overview: Lonking Holdings is a Fujian/Shanghai-rooted Chinese manufacturer of construction and material-handling machinery, best known for wheel loaders, forklifts, excavators and road rollers, with an ancillary finance-lease business supporting equipment sales. The Cayman-incorporated, HKEX-listed group reports in RMB and sells primarily through an agency-based distribution network to domestic Chinese infrastructure, mining, logistics and construction customers, with a rapidly growing export business (~34% of FY2025 revenue) spanning Belt and Road and emerging markets. Lonking is controlled by its founding family (the Li/Ngai family, via Ngai Ngan Ying and associates, holding roughly 57% of shares).

business_model.summary: Lonking manufactures and sells heavy equipment (wheel loaders, forklifts, excavators, road rollers, core components) through a network of independent sales agents in China and overseas distributors, generating revenue primarily from one-time equipment sales plus a smaller recurring stream from parts/components and finance leases. Profitability is tied to machine volumes, product mix (loaders and excavators carry higher margins than forklifts), steel/component input costs, and export pricing.
business_model.customer_type: B2B — infrastructure contractors, mining operators, logistics/warehouse operators, and construction companies, reached mainly through third-party sales agents and export distributors rather than direct B2C sale
business_model.geographic_mix: Mainland China domestic ~66% (North region ~20%, East ~14%, Central ~9%, South ~8%, Northwest ~7%, Southwest ~4%, Northeast ~3%), export/overseas ~34% of FY2025 revenue (record high, +19% YoY), with export share continuing to rise in H1 FY2026 (~30% of revenue, +21% YoY)

competitive_position.market_position: Mid-tier player in China's construction machinery industry — a long-established, profitable domestic wheel loader specialist and forklift maker, but materially smaller in scale than the dominant Chinese majors (XCMG, SANY, Zoomlion each generate multiples of Lonking's revenue) and without the global excavator/crane franchise of those peers or the premium brand positioning of Caterpillar/Komatsu

moat_factors.description: Decades of focus on wheel loaders (its largest, most profitable segment) gives Lonking manufacturing scale and a reputation for cost-effectiveness ('quality, service, cost-effectiveness') versus both Chinese and global rivals
Long-standing domestic agent network and expanding overseas distributor channels provide reach, though management itself flagged aging/inactive agents it is actively replacing

Established Chinese brand with multi-decade operating history and National Technical Committee involvement in industry standards, but brand power is weaker than XCMG/SANY/Zoomlion's global marketing scale
Industry-leading low gearing (32% gross gearing at FY2025) and a large net cash position give room to compete on financing terms and pricing versus more leveraged rivals

weaknesses: Sub-scale versus XCMG/SANY/Zoomlion, which limits R&D budget and global brand investment
Heavy reliance on wheel loaders and forklifts — two product lines facing intensifying domestic price competition and, in forklifts, below-average electrification penetration
Export growth increasingly exposed to trade-remedy actions in developed markets (e.g. UK anti-dumping duties on Chinese excavators)
Family-controlled share register (~57% held by founder-related parties) limits free float and may constrain corporate actions

growth_drivers: Overseas/export expansion — export revenue hit a record RMB3.8bn in FY2025 (+19% YoY) and continued at +21% YoY in H1 FY2026, with management targeting further growth along Belt and Road and emerging-market routes

Mix shift toward excavators — fastest-growing segment (+60% YoY in FY2025, +28% YoY in H1 FY2026), benefiting from China's equipment-renewal cycle and infrastructure stimulus under the 15th Five-Year Plan

Electrification of loaders and forklifts — management cites a surge in electric loader sales as a growth driver in FY2025 and plans to accelerate forklift electrification given below-average current penetration
Domestic equipment-replacement ('old-for-new') cycle — accumulated replacement demand from the prior sales peak and government equipment-renewal subsidies support a multi-year volume recovery

New-product rollout across emission standards/regions — a 2025 'technology deployment reform' delivered new models tailored to different international emission/regulatory standards, intended as a new growth engine
Cost/efficiency programs — ongoing procurement, production and logistics efficiency initiatives have driven multiple consecutive years of gross-margin expansion (19.6% to 21.4% FY2024→FY2025)
Potential strategic collaboration with global industry peers, as flagged in the FY2025 chairman's letter as a 2026 priority

business.description: Domestic sales (~66% of revenue) are tied to China's construction and infrastructure investment cycle; the sector only began a 'bottoming recovery' in 2025 after a multi-year downturn, and a renewed property-sector slowdown would hit volumes

business.risk: Forklift segment decline and competitive pricing pressure
business.description: Forklift revenue fell ~7% in FY2025 and ~10% in H1 FY2026 amid intense price competition and slow progress on electrification; management explicitly describes the segment as 'both volume and price declining'
Larger domestic and global peers have greater R&D budgets, broader product ranges (notably cranes and larger excavators) and stronger overseas brand recognition
Company is actively replacing aging/inactive domestic agents, which carries near-term execution risk to sales continuity even if beneficial longer-term

financial.risk: RMB-denominated reporting with growing export mix
financial.description: Export revenue (now ~30-34% of sales) creates FX translation and transaction exposure; H1 FY2026 recorded a swing to a net FX loss versus a gain in the prior-year period

financial.risk: Lengthening receivables on higher-value electric products
financial.description: Trade and long-term receivables grew faster than revenue in FY2025 and H1 FY2026 (long-term receivables +150% YoY) as customers take longer payment terms for pricier electric machines, raising working-capital and credit risk

Gross gearing ratio rose from 32.1% at FY2025 to 39.7% at H1 FY2026 and the gross debt-to-equity ratio rose from 52.7% to 62.9% YoY, though absolute debt levels remain low and interest coverage very high (751x)

regulatory.description: The UK imposed anti-dumping duties of 18.8%-83.5% on Chinese-made excavators (effective May 2025); further trade-remedy actions by other importing countries could curtail export growth, the company's key growth driver
Management's own FY2025/H1 FY2026 outlook explicitly flags 'trade protectionism, geopolitical conflicts and logistical disruptions' as overseas market risks
Group is within scope of OECD Pillar Two rules; assessed as immaterial exposure to date but could evolve

macro.description: Government 2026 GDP growth target of 4.5-5% and fiscal/monetary policy settings directly influence infrastructure spending and machinery replacement demand

As a heavy-equipment manufacturer, Lonking's cost of sales is exposed to steel and component costs; margin gains to date have come from efficiency programs that could be offset by input cost inflation

Overseas growth is increasingly dependent on resource-rich emerging markets and Belt and Road infrastructure spending, which is sensitive to commodity price cycles and those countries' own fiscal capacity

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China's construction machinery industry is in an early-stage cyclical recovery after a multi-year downturn (2021-2023), driven by equipment-renewal/replacement demand, infrastructure stimulus, and especially strong export growth; industry excavator and loader sales volumes were up over 20% YoY through mid-2026 per CCMA data, with brokerages projecting double-digit domestic growth and mid-teens export growth for 2026
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — construction machinery is a classically cyclical, capex-driven industry tightly linked to China's property/infrastructure investment cycle and, increasingly, to overseas infrastructure and mining capex cycles
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect — lower Chinese interest rates and more proactive fiscal policy support infrastructure spending and machine financing/leasing demand; Lonking itself carries minimal net debt so direct balance-sheet rate sensitivity is low
key_input_costs: Batteries and electric drivetrain components (as electrification mix rises)

recent_developments.event: H1 FY2026 interim results: revenue +19.0% YoY to RMB6,658m, net profit +22.4% YoY to RMB773m, gross margin expanded to 21.55% from 20.28%; wheel loaders grew to 47% of revenue on a domestic equipment-renewal and infrastructure-driven surge, while forklifts declined to 25% of revenue; gearing increased to 39.7% from 32.1% at FY2025-end
FY2025 final dividend of HK$0.20 per share (58% payout ratio) approved at the 28 May 2026 AGM and paid 31 July 2026, up from HK$0.13 the prior year

FY2025 annual results: revenue +9.8% YoY to RMB11,215m, net profit +27.7% YoY to RMB1,301m, gross margin rose to 21.4% from 19.6%; export revenue hit a record RMB3,806m (+19.3% YoY, ~34% of sales); cash and financial assets reached a record ~RMB9.1bn equivalent and gross gearing fell to 32%, both cited by the chairman as record highs
Goldman Sachs maintained a Hold/Neutral rating with a HK$3.00 price target on Lonking

Industry-wide: China excavator and loader sales volumes up over 20% YoY through mid-2026 (CCMA data), with export volumes growing even faster than domestic — a tailwind corroborated in Lonking's own H1 FY2026 and FY2025 results
UK Trade Remedies Authority anti-dumping duties (18.8%-83.5%) on Chinese-made excavators took effect, a sector-wide overseas regulatory risk management has flagged in its outlook commentary

items.target: Continued positive growth trajectory for H2 FY2026
items.notes: No numeric revenue guidance is given; management states market demand is 'expected to continue its positive trajectory' in both domestic and overseas markets, citing equipment renewal, infrastructure policy, and resilient Belt and Road export demand
Management expects construction machinery exports to 'sustain their strong growth momentum' despite geopolitical and trade-barrier uncertainty

items.target: No specific numeric target disclosed; H1 FY2026 capex was RMB75m, up from RMB29m in H1 FY2025
items.notes: Capex funded from internal resources and general borrowings, described as supporting 'strategic transformation and product transformation'
Referenced from the Chinese government's own 2026 target as the macro backdrop management expects to support construction machinery demand

guidance.management_commentary: Management's FY2025 and H1 FY2026 outlook sections emphasize three 'core opportunities': the domestic equipment-renewal cyclical upturn, continued overseas market expansion, and substitution of conventional products by new-energy (electric) equipment. They reiterate a focus on the four core product categories (loaders, forklifts, excavators, road machinery) and continued margin, cost and service improvements, while acknowledging overseas trade protectionism and geopolitical risk as headwinds to the export growth thesis.

bull_case: Export business at record highs and still growing >19-21% YoY, diversifying away from a purely domestic-cyclical China revenue base and capturing global share gains for Chinese machinery brands

Structural mix shift toward higher-margin, faster-growing excavators (+60% YoY FY2025, +28% YoY H1 FY2026) is lifting group gross margin, which has expanded for multiple consecutive periods (19.6%→21.4%→21.55%)

Very conservative balance sheet with industry-leading gearing (32% gross gearing at FY2025-end) and a large net cash/financial-assets position (~RMB9bn+ equivalent), funding a rising dividend (payout ratio 58% in FY2025, up from prior year) with room for further capital returns

China's construction machinery industry is in the early stages of a multi-year replacement/upgrade cycle after a 2021-2023 downturn, with government fiscal stimulus and equipment-renewal subsidies providing a multi-year domestic tailwind

Electrification of loaders already a meaningful growth driver, and management is targeting the same transition in forklifts, where current penetration lags the industry — a call option on further margin and volume upside
bear_case: Forklift segment — still roughly a quarter to a third of revenue — is shrinking under price competition and slow progress on electrification, acting as a persistent drag on group growth

Sub-scale relative to XCMG, SANY and Zoomlion, which have far larger revenue bases, R&D budgets and global brand/service networks, structurally limiting Lonking's ability to win share in bigger-ticket categories like cranes and large excavators

Export growth, now the main growth engine, is directly exposed to rising trade protectionism — the UK's 18.8%-83.5% anti-dumping duties on Chinese excavators illustrate a risk that could spread to other markets and compress the export margin/volume thesis

Domestic recovery is still described by management itself as a 'bottoming recovery' rather than a confirmed new upcycle, leaving the company exposed if China's property/infrastructure investment disappoints again

Rising receivables (trade and especially long-term receivables, as customers take extended terms on pricier electric machines) and a jump in gearing (32%→39.7% gross gearing within six months) bear watching as leading indicators of credit or working-capital strain if growth decelerates
Family-controlled share register (~57% held by the Ngai/Li family interests) concentrates governance power and limits free float, a structural overhang for some institutional investors
